questions.text: If $z_1, z_2, z_3\in\mathbb{C}$ are the vertices of an equilateral triangle, whose centroid is $z_0$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{3}\left(z_k-z_0\right)^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
About the centroid the vertices are $w$, $w\omega$, $w\omega^2$, where $w=z_1-z_0$ and $\omega$ is a complex cube root of unity.
$\displaystyle\sum(z_k-z_0)^2=w^2(1+\omega^2+\omega^4)=w^2(1+\omega+\omega^2)=0$.

questions.text: The sum $1+\dfrac{1+3}{2!}+\dfrac{1+3+5}{3!}+\dfrac{1+3+5+7}{4!}+\ldots$ upto $\infty$ terms, is equal to
questions.sol:
The $n$th numerator is $1+3+\cdots+(2n-1)=n^2$, so the sum is $\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n^2}{n!}=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{n}{(n-1)!}$.
$\dfrac{n}{(n-1)!}=\dfrac{1}{(n-2)!}+\dfrac{1}{(n-1)!}$ (first term only for $n\ge2$), giving $e+e=2e$.

questions.text: Line $L_1$ of slope 2 and line $L_2$ of slope $\dfrac12$ intersect at the origin O. In the first quadrant, $P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_{12}$ are 12 points on line $L_1$ and $Q_1, Q_2, \ldots, Q_9$ are 9 points on line $L_2$. Then the total number of triangles, that can be formed having vertices at three of the 22 points O, $P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_{12}$, $Q_1, Q_2, \ldots, Q_9$, is:
questions.sol:
O and the $P$s are 13 collinear points; O and the $Q$s are 10 collinear points.
Triangles $=\binom{22}{3}-\binom{13}{3}-\binom{10}{3}=1540-286-120=1134$.

questions.text:
If the probability that the random variable $X$ takes the value $x$ is given by
$P(X=x)=k(x+1)3^{-x}$, $x=0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots$, where $k$ is a constant, then $P(X\ge3)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\displaystyle\sum_{x\ge0}(x+1)\left(\frac13\right)^x=\frac{1}{(1-1/3)^2}=\frac94$, so $k=\dfrac49$.
$P(X\le2)=\dfrac49\left(1+\dfrac23+\dfrac13\right)=\dfrac89$, so $P(X\ge3)=\dfrac19$.

questions.text: Consider the lines $x(3\lambda+1)+y(7\lambda+2)=17\lambda+5$, $\lambda$ being a parameter, all passing through a point P. One of these lines (say $L$) is farthest from the origin. If the distance of $L$ from the point $(3, 6)$ is $d$, then the value of $d^2$ is
questions.sol:
Rewrite as $(x+2y-5)+\lambda(3x+7y-17)=0$; both brackets vanish at $P(1,2)$.
The line through P farthest from O is perpendicular to OP: $x+2y=5$.
$d=\dfrac{|3+12-5|}{\sqrt5}=\dfrac{10}{\sqrt5}$, so $d^2=20$.

questions.text: Let $C$ be the circle of minimum area enclosing the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ with eccentricity $\dfrac12$ and foci $(\pm2, 0)$. Let $PQR$ be a variable triangle, whose vertex $P$ is on the circle $C$ and the side $QR$ of length $2a$ is parallel to the major axis of $E$ and contains the point of intersection of $E$ with the negative $y$-axis. Then the maximum area of the triangle $PQR$ is :
questions.sol:
$ae=2$ with $e=\dfrac12$ gives $a=4$, $b^2=16-4=12$. The smallest enclosing circle is $x^2+y^2=16$.
QR lies on $y=-2\sqrt3$ and has length 8. P is farthest from this line at $(0,4)$, at height $4+2\sqrt3$.
Maximum area $=\dfrac12\times8\times(4+2\sqrt3)=8(2+\sqrt3)$.

questions.text: The number of solutions of the equation $\left(4-\sqrt{3}\right)\sin x-2\sqrt{3}\cos^2x=-\dfrac{4}{1+\sqrt{3}}$, $x\in\left[-2\pi, \dfrac{5\pi}{2}\right]$ is
questions.sol:
$-\dfrac{4}{1+\sqrt3}=2-2\sqrt3$. With $s=\sin x$: $2\sqrt3s^2+(4-\sqrt3)s-2=0$.
The discriminant is $(4-\sqrt3)^2+16\sqrt3=(4+\sqrt3)^2$, so $s=\dfrac12$ or $s=-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}$ (rejected).
$\sin x=\dfrac12$ in $\left[-2\pi,\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\right]$: $-\dfrac{11\pi}{6}, -\dfrac{7\pi}{6}, \dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{5\pi}{6}, \dfrac{13\pi}{6}$: 5 solutions.

questions.text: Each of the angles $\beta$ and $\gamma$ that a given line makes with the positive $y$- and $z$-axes, respectively, is half of the angle that this line makes with the positive $x$-axes. Then the sum of all possible values of the angle $\beta$ is
questions.sol:
With $\alpha=2\beta=2\gamma$: $\cos^2\alpha+2\cos^2\dfrac{\alpha}{2}=1$, i.e. $\cos^2\alpha+1+\cos\alpha=1$, so $\cos\alpha=0$ or $-1$.
$\alpha=\dfrac\pi2$ gives $\beta=\dfrac\pi4$; $\alpha=\pi$ gives $\beta=\dfrac\pi2$.
Sum $=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.

questions.text: The distance of the point $(7, 10, 11)$ from the line $\dfrac{x-4}{1}=\dfrac{y-4}{0}=\dfrac{z-2}{3}$ along the line $\dfrac{x-9}{2}=\dfrac{y-13}{3}=\dfrac{z-17}{6}$ is
questions.sol:
Move from $(7,10,11)$ along $(2,3,6)$ (length 7): $(7+2t, 10+3t, 11+6t)$.
The first line has $y=4$, so $t=-2$, giving $(3,4,-1)$; check: $\dfrac{3-4}{1}=\dfrac{-1-2}{3}=-1$.
Distance $=|t|\times7=14$.

questions.text: Let $f: \mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function defined by $f(x)=\big||x+2|-2|x|\big|$. If $m$ is the number of points of local minima and $n$ is the number of points of local maxima of $f$, then $m+n$ is
questions.sol:
$g(x)=|x+2|-2|x|$ is $x-2$ for $x<-2$, $3x+2$ on $[-2,0]$ and $2-x$ for $x>0$; $f=|g|$.
$f$ decreases on $\left(-\infty,-\dfrac23\right]$ (no turn at $-2$), is 0 at $-\dfrac23$, rises to 2 at $x=0$, falls to 0 at $x=2$ and then rises.
Local minima at $-\dfrac23$ and 2, local maximum at 0: $m+n=3$.

questions.text: The shortest distance between the curves $y^2=8x$ and $x^2+y^2+12y+35=0$ is:
questions.sol:
The circle has centre $(0,-6)$ and radius 1. For $(2t^2, 4t)$ on the parabola, $D^2=4t^4+(4t+6)^2$.
$\dfrac{d}{dt}D^2=16t^3+8(4t+6)=0$ gives $t^3+2t+3=0$, $t=-1$, so $D^2=4+4=8$.
Shortest distance $=2\sqrt2-1$.

questions.text: The integral $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\frac{8x\,dx}{4\cos^2x+\sin^2x}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Replacing $x$ by $\pi-x$: $I=4\pi\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\frac{dx}{4\cos^2x+\sin^2x}=8\pi\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sec^2x\,dx}{4+\tan^2x}$.
$=8\pi\cdot\dfrac12\left[\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\tan x}{2}\right]_0^{\pi/2}=8\pi\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{4}=2\pi^2$.

questions.text: The area of the region $\left\{(x, y): |x-y|\le y\le4\sqrt{x}\right\}$ is
questions.sol:
$|x-y|\le y$ means $y\ge0$ and $y\ge\dfrac x2$. So the region is $\dfrac x2\le y\le4\sqrt x$, which closes where $\dfrac x2=4\sqrt x$, i.e. $x=64$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_0^{64}\left(4\sqrt x-\frac x2\right)dx=\frac83\cdot512-1024=\frac{1024}{3}$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+3\left(\tan^2x\right)y+3y=\sec^2x$, $y(0)=\dfrac13+e^3$. Then $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\tan^2x+1=\sec^2x$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+3\sec^2x\,y=\sec^2x$. Integrating factor $e^{3\tan x}$.
$ye^{3\tan x}=\dfrac13e^{3\tan x}+C$; $y(0)$ gives $C=e^3$, so $y=\dfrac13+e^{3-3\tan x}$.
$y\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)=\dfrac13+1=\dfrac43$.

questions.text: Let I be the identity matrix of order $3\times3$ and for the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}\lambda&2&3\\4&5&6\\7&-1&2\end{bmatrix}$, $|A|=-1$. Let $B$ be the inverse of the matrix $\operatorname{adj}\left(A\operatorname{adj}\left(A^2\right)\right)$. Then $|(\lambda B+I)|$ is equal to __________
questions.note: NTA's final key accepts 38 or $-38$: the determinant is $-38$, and 38 is its modulus (the bars can be read either way).
questions.sol:
$|A|=16\lambda-49=-1$, so $\lambda=3$.
$A\operatorname{adj}(A^2)=A(\operatorname{adj}A)^2=|A|\operatorname{adj}A=-\operatorname{adj}A$; $\operatorname{adj}(-\operatorname{adj}A)=\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)=|A|A=-A$. So $B=-A^{-1}$.
$\lambda B+I=I-3A^{-1}=A^{-1}(A-3I)$, and $|A-3I|=\begin{vmatrix}0&2&3\\4&2&6\\7&-1&-1\end{vmatrix}=92-54=38$.
$|\lambda B+I|=\dfrac{38}{-1}=-38$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$, $\vec{c}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{d}$ be a vector such that $\vec{b}\times\vec{d}=\vec{c}\times\vec{d}$ and $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d}=4$. Then $\left|\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{d}\right)\right|^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$(\vec b-\vec c)\times\vec d=\vec0$, so $\vec d=t(\hat i-2\hat j+\hat k)$; $\vec a\cdot\vec d=-2t=4$ gives $t=-2$, $\vec d=-2\hat i+4\hat j-2\hat k$.
$\vec a\times\vec d=-8\hat i+8\hat k$, so $|\vec a\times\vec d|^2=128$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\left(\frac{\tan x}{x}\right)^{\frac{1}{x^2}}=p$, then $96\log_ep$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{\tan x}{x}=1+\dfrac{x^2}{3}+\cdots$, so $\log_ep=\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1}{x^2}\cdot\frac{x^2}{3}=\frac13$.
$96\log_ep=32$.

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-ILIST-II
A. Boltzmann constantI. $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-1}}$
B. Coefficient of viscosityII. $\mathrm{MLT^{-3}K^{-1}}$
C. Planck's constantIII. $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}}$
D. Thermal conductivityIV. $\mathrm{ML^{-1}T^{-1}}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II
A - III, B - II, C - I, D - IV
A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I
A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I
questions.sol:
Boltzmann constant = energy/temperature: $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}}$ (III). Viscosity = stress/velocity gradient: $\mathrm{ML^{-1}T^{-1}}$ (IV).
Planck's constant = energy $\times$ time: $\mathrm{ML^2T^{-1}}$ (I). Thermal conductivity $=\dfrac{\text{power}\times\text{length}}{\text{area}\times\text{temperature}}$: $\mathrm{MLT^{-3}K^{-1}}$ (II).

questions.text:
A particle is projected with velocity $u$ so that its horizontal range is three times the maximum height attained by it. The horizontal range of the projectile is given as $\dfrac{nu^2}{25g}$, where value of $n$ is:
(Given, '$g$' is the acceleration due to gravity.)
questions.sol:
$R=3H$: $\dfrac{2u^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}=\dfrac{3u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$, so $\tan\theta=\dfrac43$ and $\sin2\theta=\dfrac{24}{25}$.
$R=\dfrac{u^2\sin2\theta}{g}=\dfrac{24u^2}{25g}$, so $n=24$.

questions.text:
A particle moves along the $x$-axis and has its displacement $x$ varying with time t according to the equation:
$x=c_0(t^2-2)+c(t-2)^2$
where $c_0$ and c are constants of appropriate dimensions.
Then, which of the following statements is correct?
options: the initial velocity of the particle is 4c
the acceleration of the particle is $2c_0$
the acceleration of the particle is 2c
the acceleration of the particle is $2(c+c_0)$
questions.sol:
$v=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2c_0t+2c(t-2)$, so the initial velocity is $-4c$ (option 1 is wrong).
$a=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=2c_0+2c=2(c+c_0)$.

questions.text: Consider two blocks A and B of masses $m_1$ = 10 kg and $m_2$ = 5 kg that are placed on a frictionless table. The block A moves with a constant speed $v$ = 3 m/s towards the block B kept at rest. A spring with spring constant k = 3000 N/m is attached with the block B as shown in the figure. After the collision, suppose that the blocks A and B, along with the spring in constant compression state, move together, then the compression in the spring is, (Neglect the mass of the spring)
questions.sol:
Common velocity: $V=\dfrac{10\times3}{15}=2$ m/s.
Kinetic energy lost $=\dfrac12(10)(9)-\dfrac12(15)(4)=45-30=15$ J, stored in the spring.
$\dfrac12kx^2=15$: $x^2=\dfrac{30}{3000}=0.01$, $x=0.1$ m.

questions.text:
Two cylindrical vessels of equal cross sectional area of 2m$^2$ contain water upto heights 10m and 6m, respectively. If the vessels are connected at their bottom then the work done by the force of gravity is
(Density of water is $10^3$ kg/m$^3$ and g = 10 m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
The common final level is 8 m. A column of height $h$ has potential energy $\rho Ag\dfrac{h^2}{2}$.
Initial: $10^3\times2\times10\times\dfrac{100+36}{2}=1.36\times10^6$ J. Final: $10^3\times2\times10\times\dfrac{64+64}{2}=1.28\times10^6$ J.
Work by gravity = loss of potential energy $=8\times10^4$ J.

questions.text: A block of mass 1 kg, moving along $x$ with speed $v_i$ = 10 m/s enters a rough region ranging from $x$ = 0.1 m to $x$ = 1.9 m. The retarding force acting on the block in this range is $F_r=-kx$ N, with k = 10 N/m. Then the final speed of the block as it crosses rough region is.
questions.sol:
Work done by the retarding force $=-\displaystyle\int_{0.1}^{1.9}10x\,dx=-5(3.61-0.01)=-18$ J.
$\dfrac12v_f^2=50-18=32$, so $v_f=8$ m/s.

questions.text: A solid steel ball of diameter 3.6 mm acquired terminal velocity $2.45\times10^{-2}$ m/s while falling under gravity through an oil of density 925 kg m$^{-3}$. Take density of steel as 7825 kg m$^{-3}$ and g as 9.8 m/s$^2$. The viscosity of the oil in SI unit is
questions.sol:
$\eta=\dfrac{2r^2(\rho-\sigma)g}{9v_t}$ with $r=1.8\times10^{-3}$ m.
$\eta=\dfrac{2\times3.24\times10^{-6}\times6900\times9.8}{9\times2.45\times10^{-2}}=\dfrac{0.4382}{0.2205}\approx1.99$ Pa s.

questions.text: An ideal gas exists in a state with pressure $P_0$, volume $V_0$. It is isothermally expanded to 4 times of its initial volume($V_0$), then isobarically compressed to its original volume. Finally the system is heated isochorically to bring it to its initial state. The amount of heat exchanged in this process is
questions.sol:
For the cycle $\Delta U=0$, so the net heat equals the net work.
Isothermal expansion: $P_0V_0\ln4=2\ln2\,P_0V_0$. Isobaric compression at $\dfrac{P_0}{4}$ from $4V_0$ to $V_0$: $-\dfrac{P_0}{4}\times3V_0=-0.75P_0V_0$. Isochoric step: 0.
Net heat $=P_0V_0(2\ln2-0.75)$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Pressure of an ideal gas, contained in a closed vessel, is increased by 0.4% when heated by 1$^\circ$C. Its initial temperature must be:
questions.sol:
At constant volume $P\propto T$, so $\dfrac{\Delta P}{P}=\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}$.
$0.004=\dfrac{1}{T}$, so $T=250$ K.

questions.text: In the resonance experiment, two air columns (closed at one end) of 100 cm and 120 cm long, give 15 beats per second when each one is sounding in the respective fundamental modes. The velocity of sound in the air column is:
questions.sol:
Fundamental of a closed pipe: $f=\dfrac{v}{4L}$.
$\dfrac{v}{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{1.00}-\dfrac{1}{1.20}\right)=\dfrac{v}{24}=15$, so $v=360$ m/s.

questions.text: A magnetic dipole experiences a torque of $80\sqrt{3}$ N m when placed in uniform magnetic field in such a way that dipole moment makes angle of 60$^\circ$ with magnetic field. The potential energy of the dipole is :
questions.sol:
$\tau=mB\sin60^\circ=80\sqrt3$, so $mB=160$ N m.
$U=-mB\cos60^\circ=-80$ J.

questions.text: An electric bulb rated as 100W-220V is connected to an ac source of rms voltage 220V. The peak value of current through the bulb is :
questions.sol:
$I_{rms}=\dfrac{P}{V_{rms}}=\dfrac{100}{220}=0.455$ A.

questions.text: Using a battery, a 100 pF capacitor is charged to 60 V and then the battery is removed. After that, a second uncharged capacitor is connected to the first capacitor in parallel. If the final voltage across the second capacitor is 20 V, its capacitance is: (in pF)
questions.sol:
Charge is conserved: $Q=100\times60=6000$ pC.
Common voltage 20 V: $100+C=\dfrac{6000}{20}=300$, so $C=200$ pF.

questions.text: A motor operating on 100 V draws a current of 1 A. If the efficiency of the motor is 91.6%, then the loss of power in units of cal/s is
questions.sol:
Input power $=100$ W; loss $=8.4\%$ of it $=8.4$ W $=8.4$ J/s.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A : If Oxygen ion $(\mathrm{O^{-2}})$ and Hydrogen ion $(\mathrm{H^+})$ enter normal to the magnetic field with equal momentum, then the path of $\mathrm{O^{-2}}$ ion has a smaller curvature than that of $\mathrm{H^+}$.
Reason R : A proton with same linear momentum as an electron will form a path of smaller radius of curvature on entering a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.note: NTA's final key gives option (3). $r=\dfrac{p}{qB}$, so with equal momentum the $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ ion (charge $2e$) moves on a circle of half the radius of the $\mathrm{H^+}$ path; Assertion A is true if "smaller curvature" is read as smaller radius of curvature, as the key does (strictly, curvature $=1/r$ is larger).
questions.sol:
In a perpendicular field $r=\dfrac{p}{qB}$.
Equal momentum: $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ has twice the charge of $\mathrm{H^+}$, so its radius of curvature is half as large; A is taken as true in this sense (see the note).
A proton and an electron have equal charge magnitude, so with equal momentum their radii are equal: R is false.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two monochromatic light beams have intensities in the ratio 1:9. An interference pattern is obtained by these beams. The ratio of the intensities of maximum to minimum is
questions.sol:
Amplitudes are in the ratio $1:3$.
$\dfrac{I_{max}}{I_{min}}=\dfrac{(3+1)^2}{(3-1)^2}=\dfrac{16}{4}=4:1$.

questions.text: A monochromatic light of frequency $5\times10^{14}$ Hz travelling through air, is incident on a medium of refractive index '2'. Wavelength of the refracted light will be :
questions.sol: In air $\lambda=\dfrac{3\times10^8}{5\times10^{14}}=600$ nm. The frequency is unchanged on refraction, so in the medium $\lambda=\dfrac{600}{2}=300$ nm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Width of one of the two slits in a Young's double slit interference experiment is half of the other slit. The ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in the interference pattern is :
questions.sol:
Intensity from a slit is proportional to its width: $I_1:I_2=1:2$, amplitudes $1:\sqrt2$.
$\dfrac{I_{max}}{I_{min}}=\dfrac{(\sqrt2+1)^2}{(\sqrt2-1)^2}=\dfrac{3+2\sqrt2}{3-2\sqrt2}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A : The Bohr model is applicable to hydrogen and hydrogen-like atoms only.
Reason R : The formulation of Bohr model does not include repulsive force between electrons.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.sol:
Bohr's model treats a single electron moving in the field of the nucleus, so it works only for one-electron (hydrogen-like) species: A is true.
It has no term for the repulsion between electrons, which is exactly why it fails for many-electron atoms: R is true and explains A.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The truth table corresponding to the circuit given below is :
questions.sol:
The OR gate gives $A+B$; the AND gate combines it with A: $C=A\cdot(A+B)=A$.
So C copies A: $C=0, 0, 1, 1$ for $(A,B)=(0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1)$, which is table (1).

questions.text:
A physical quantity C is related to four other quantities p, q, r and s as follows
$C=\dfrac{pq^2}{r^3\sqrt{s}}$.
The percentage errors in the measurement of p, q, r and s are 1%, 2%, 3% and 2%, respectively. The percentage error in the measurement of C will be __________ %.
questions.sol: $\dfrac{\Delta C}{C}=\dfrac{\Delta p}{p}+2\dfrac{\Delta q}{q}+3\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}+\dfrac12\dfrac{\Delta s}{s}=1+4+9+1=15\%$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble A in air is half the excess pressure inside another soap bubble B in air. If the volume of the bubble A is $n$ times the volume of the bubble B, then, the value of $n$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Excess pressure in a soap bubble $=\dfrac{4T}{r}$, so half the excess pressure means twice the radius: $r_A=2r_B$.
$n=\left(\dfrac{r_A}{r_B}\right)^3=8$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two cells of emfs 1 V and 2 V and internal resistances 2 $\Omega$ and 1 $\Omega$, respectively, are connected in series with an external resistance of 6 $\Omega$. The total current in the circuit is $I_1$. Now the same two cells in parallel configuration are connected to same external resistance. In this case, the total current drawn is $I_2$. The value of $\left(\dfrac{I_1}{I_2}\right)$ is $\dfrac{x}{3}$. The value of $x$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Series: $I_1=\dfrac{1+2}{2+1+6}=\dfrac13$ A.
Parallel: $E_{eq}=\dfrac{1/2+2/1}{1/2+1/1}=\dfrac53$ V, $r_{eq}=\dfrac23\ \Omega$, so $I_2=\dfrac{5/3}{6+2/3}=\dfrac14$ A.
$\dfrac{I_1}{I_2}=\dfrac43$, so $x=4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Light from a point source in air falls on a spherical glass surface (refractive index, $\mu$=1.5 and radius of curvature = 50 cm). The image is formed at a distance of 200 cm from the glass surface inside the glass. The magnitude of distance of the light source from the glass surface is __________ m.
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{\mu_2}{v}-\dfrac{\mu_1}{u}=\dfrac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R}$: $\dfrac{1.5}{200}-\dfrac1u=\dfrac{0.5}{50}$.
$\dfrac1u=0.0075-0.01=-0.0025$, so $u=-400$ cm; the distance is 4 m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electron in the hydrogen atom initially in the fourth excited state makes a transition to n$^{\text{th}}$ energy state by emitting a photon of energy 2.86 eV. The integer value of n will be __________.
questions.sol:
The fourth excited state is $n=5$: $E_5=-\dfrac{13.6}{25}=-0.544$ eV.
Final energy $=-0.544-2.86=-3.40$ eV $=-\dfrac{13.6}{4}$, so $n=2$.

questions.text:
Mass of magnesium required to produce 220 mL of hydrogen gas at STP on reaction with excess of dil. HCl is
Given: Molar mass of Mg is 24 g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Mg+2HCl\rightarrow MgCl_2+H_2}$: 1 mol Mg gives 1 mol $\mathrm{H_2}$ (22400 mL at STP).
Moles of $\mathrm{H_2}=\dfrac{220}{22400}=9.82\times10^{-3}$; mass of Mg $=9.82\times10^{-3}\times24=0.2357$ g $\approx236$ mg.

questions.text: For electrons in '2s' and '2p' orbitals, the orbital angular momentum values, respectively are :
questions.sol:
Orbital angular momentum $=\sqrt{l(l+1)}\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$.
2s: $l=0$, value 0. 2p: $l=1$, value $\sqrt2\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : When a system containing ice in equilibrium with water (liquid) is heated, heat is absorbed by the system and there is no change in the temperature of the system until whole ice gets melted.
Statement II : At melting point of ice, there is absorption of heat in order to overcome intermolecular forces of attraction within the molecules of water in ice and kinetic energy of molecules is not increased at melting point.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
While ice and water coexist, the heat supplied (latent heat) melts the ice and the temperature stays at the melting point: I is true.
This heat is used to overcome the attractions (hydrogen bonds) holding the molecules in the solid; as the temperature is constant, the average kinetic energy does not rise: II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: 10 mL of 2 M NaOH solution is added to 20 mL of 1 M HCl solution kept in a beaker. Now, 10 mL of this mixture is poured into a volumetric flask of 100 mL containing 2 moles of HCl and made the volume upto the mark with distilled water. The solution in this flask is :
questions.sol:
NaOH (0.02 mol) exactly neutralises HCl (0.02 mol), so the 10 mL portion added is only NaCl solution and brings no acid or base.
The flask therefore contains 2 mol HCl in 100 mL: $\dfrac{2}{0.1}=20$ M HCl.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: 40 mL of a mixture of $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ and HCl (aqueous solution) is titrated against 0.1 M NaOH solution conductometrically. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ is neutralised first followed by neutralisation of HCl
The concentration of HCl in the original mixture is 0.005 M
The concentration of $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ in the original mixture is 0.005 M
Point 'C' indicates the complete neutralisation of HCl
questions.sol:
The strong acid HCl reacts first: fast $\mathrm{H^+}$ ions are replaced by $\mathrm{Na^+}$, so conductance falls to B (2.0 mL). Then acetic acid is neutralised (B to C, 5.0 mL), after which excess NaOH raises it steeply.
HCl: $0.1\times2.0=0.2$ mmol in 40 mL, i.e. 0.005 M. $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$: $0.1\times3.0=0.3$ mmol, i.e. 0.0075 M; C marks the end of acetic acid.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The standard cell potential $\left(E^\ominus_{\text{cell}}\right)$ of a fuel cell based on the oxidation of methanol in air that has been used to power television relay station is measured as 1.21 V. The standard half cell reduction potential for $\mathrm{O_2}$ $\left(E^\circ_{\mathrm{O_2/H_2O}}\right)$ is 1.229 V.
Choose the correct statement:
options: Oxygen is formed at the anode.
Reduction of methanol takes place at the cathode.
The standard half cell reduction potential for the reduction of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ $\left(E^\circ_{\mathrm{CO_2/CH_3OH}}\right)$ is 19 mV
Reactants are fed at one go to each electrode.
questions.sol:
Methanol is oxidised at the anode and oxygen is reduced at the cathode; reactants are fed continuously (options 1, 2, 4 wrong).
$E^\circ_{cell}=E^\circ_{\mathrm{O_2/H_2O}}-E^\circ_{\mathrm{CO_2/CH_3OH}}$, so $E^\circ_{\mathrm{CO_2/CH_3OH}}=1.229-1.21=0.019$ V $=19$ mV.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following statements related to temperature dependence of rate constants.
Identify the correct statements.
A. The Arrhenius equation holds true only for an elementary homogenous reaction.
B. The unit of A is same as that of k in Arrhenius equation.
C. At a given temperature, a low activation energy means a fast reaction.
D. A and Ea as used in Arrhenius equation depend on temperature.
E. When Ea >> RT, A and Ea become interdependent.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: false; the equation also describes complex and heterogeneous reactions. B: true; $e^{-E_a/RT}$ is dimensionless, so A has the units of k.
C: true; a smaller $E_a$ gives a larger $e^{-E_a/RT}$ and a larger k. D: false; A and $E_a$ are treated as constants, nearly independent of temperature.
E: false; A and $E_a$ are independent parameters. Hence B and C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : Wet cotton clothes made of cellulose based carbohydrate takes comparatively longer time to get dried than wet nylon polymer based clothes.
Statement II : Intermolecular hydrogen bonding with water molecule is more in nylon-based clothes than in the case of cotton clothes.
In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Cellulose carries many $-\mathrm{OH}$ groups that hydrogen-bond strongly with water, so cotton holds water longer and dries more slowly: I is true.
Nylon has far fewer such sites per unit mass, so its hydrogen bonding with water is less, not more: II is false.

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-I
(Family)		LIST-II
(Symbol of Element)
A. Pnictogen (group 15)I. Ts
B. ChalcogenII. Og
C. HalogenIII. Lv
D. Noble gasIV. Mc
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Moscovium (Mc, Z = 115) is in group 15 (IV); livermorium (Lv, 116) is a chalcogen (III).
Tennessine (Ts, 117) is a halogen (I); oganesson (Og, 118) is a noble gas (II).

questions.text:
The correct orders among the following are
Atomic radius : B < Al < Ga < In < Tl
Electronegativity : Al < Ga < In < Tl < B
Density : Tl < In < Ga < Al < B
1st Ionisation Energy : In < Al < Ga < Tl < B
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
The four orders are unlabelled in the paper; taken as A to D in the order printed.
A: false; Ga (135 pm) is smaller than Al (143 pm) because of poor shielding by the 3d electrons. B: true (Al 1.5, Ga 1.6, In 1.7, Tl 1.8, B 2.0).
C: false; density increases down the group (B lightest, Tl densest). D: true (In 558, Al 577, Ga 579, Tl 589, B 801 kJ mol$^{-1}$). Hence B and D.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : $\mathrm{CrO_3}$ is a stronger oxidizing agent than $\mathrm{MoO_3}$
Statement II : Cr(VI) is more stable than Mo(VI)
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Down a transition group the higher oxidation states become more stable, so Mo(VI) is more stable than Cr(VI): II is false.
Because Cr(VI) is less stable, it is readily reduced; $\mathrm{CrO_3}$ is the stronger oxidising agent: I is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the diamagnetic octahedral complex ions from below ;
A. $\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}}$
B. $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$
C. $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}$
D. $\mathrm{[Co(H_2O)_3F_3]}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: Mn(III), $d^4$, low spin $t_{2g}^4$: 2 unpaired, paramagnetic. B: Co(III), $d^6$, low spin $t_{2g}^6$: diamagnetic.
C: Fe(II), $d^6$ with strong-field $\mathrm{CN^-}$: $t_{2g}^6$, diamagnetic. D: Co(III) with weak-field $\mathrm{F^-}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}$: high spin, 4 unpaired.
Hence B and C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Compounds that should not be used as primary standards in titrimetric analysis are :
A. $\mathrm{Na_2Cr_2O_7}$
B. Oxalic acid
C. NaOH
D. $\mathrm{FeSO_4\cdot6H_2O}$
E. Sodium tetraborate
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A primary standard must be pure, stable in air and non-hygroscopic, so that it can be weighed exactly.
$\mathrm{Na_2Cr_2O_7}$ (hygroscopic; $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ is used instead), NaOH (absorbs moisture and $\mathrm{CO_2}$) and $\mathrm{FeSO_4\cdot6H_2O}$ (oxidised by air; Mohr's salt is used instead) are unsuitable.
Oxalic acid and sodium tetraborate (borax) are standard primary standards. Hence A, C and D.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
In Dumas' method for estimation of nitrogen 0.4 g of an organic compound gave 60 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K temperature and 715 mm Hg pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound is
(Given : Aqueous tension at 300 K = 15 mm Hg)
questions.sol:
Pressure of dry $\mathrm{N_2}=715-15=700$ mm Hg. Volume at STP $=60\times\dfrac{700}{760}\times\dfrac{273}{300}=50.3$ mL.
Mass of $\mathrm{N_2}=\dfrac{50.3}{22400}\times28=0.0629$ g.
Percentage $=\dfrac{0.0629}{0.4}\times100\approx15.71\%$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : Hyperconjugation is not a permanent effect.
Statement II : In general, greater the number of alkyl groups attached to a positively charged C-atom, greater is the hyperconjugation interaction and stabilization of the cation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Hyperconjugation (delocalisation of C-H $\sigma$ electrons) is a permanent, general stabilising interaction in the molecule: I is false.
More alkyl groups on the cationic carbon provide more $\alpha$ C-H bonds for hyperconjugation, so stability rises ($3^\circ>2^\circ>1^\circ$): II is true.

questions.text: What is the correct IUPAC name of the compound below ?
questions.sol:
The parent is benzoic acid, with the $-\mathrm{COOH}$ carbon as C1. Going round towards the $-\mathrm{OH}$: OH at C2, Br at C3 and $\mathrm{NO_2}$ at C5.
Prefixes go in alphabetical order (bromo, hydroxy, nitro): 3-bromo-2-hydroxy-5-nitrobenzoic acid.

questions.text: In the following series of reactions identify the major products A & B respectively
questions.sol:
Br is an ortho/para director, and the bulky $-\mathrm{SO_3H}$ group enters mainly para: A is 4-bromobenzenesulphonic acid.
In A, Br directs ortho to itself and $-\mathrm{SO_3H}$ directs meta to itself; both point to the same position, next to Br.
B is 3,4-dibromobenzenesulphonic acid, option (4).

questions.text: The major product (P) in the following reaction is :
questions.sol:
Phenylglyoxal, $\mathrm{Ph{-}CO{-}CHO}$, has no $\alpha$-hydrogen; with hot KOH it undergoes an intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction.
Hydroxide adds to the CHO group, and a hydride moves to the neighbouring keto carbon: the CHO becomes $\mathrm{COO^-}$ and the C=O becomes CH(OH).
P is potassium mandelate, $\mathrm{Ph{-}CH(OH){-}COO^-K^+}$.

questions.text: The sequence from the following that would result in giving predominantly 3, 4, 5-Tribromoaniline is :
questions.sol:
In 4-nitroaniline the $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ group directs excess bromine to both positions ortho to it: 2,6-dibromo-4-nitroaniline.
Diazotisation and CuBr (Sandmeyer) replace $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ by Br, giving 1,2,3-tribromo-5-nitrobenzene; Sn/HCl then reduces $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ to $-\mathrm{NH_2}$: 3,4,5-tribromoaniline.
(1) gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline; (2) and (4) do not give the 3,4,5-pattern.

questions.text:
Fat soluble vitamins are:
A. Vitamin $\mathrm{B_1}$
B. Vitamin C
C. Vitamin E
D. Vitamin $\mathrm{B_{12}}$
E. Vitamin K
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble; the B group and C are water soluble.
Hence C (vitamin E) and E (vitamin K).

questions.text:
A perfect gas (0.1 mol) having $\bar{C}_v$ = 1.50R (independent of temperature) undergoes the above transformation from point 1 to point 4. If each step is reversible, the total work done (w) while going from point 1 to point 4 is ($-$) __________ J (nearest integer)
[Given: R = 0.082 L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
questions.sol:
Steps 1 to 2 and 3 to 4 are at constant volume: no work.
Step 2 to 3 is an expansion at 3.00 atm from 1000 to 2000 cm$^3$: $w=-P\Delta V=-3.00\times1.000$ L atm $=-3.00\times101.3$ J $\approx-304$ J.
So $w=-304$ J.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A sample of n-octane (1.14 g) was completely burnt in excess of oxygen in a bomb calorimeter, whose heat capacity is 5 kJ K$^{-1}$. As a result of combustion reaction, the temperature of the calorimeter is increased by 5 K. The magnitude of the heat of combustion of octane at constant volume is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.sol:
Heat released $=5\times5=25$ kJ. Moles of octane ($\mathrm{C_8H_{18}}$, 114 g mol$^{-1}$) $=\dfrac{1.14}{114}=0.01$.
$|\Delta U|=\dfrac{25}{0.01}=2500$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Among, Sc, Mn, Co and Cu, identify the element with highest enthalpy of atomisation. The spin only magnetic moment value of that element in its +2 oxidation state is __________ BM (in nearest integer).
questions.sol:
Enthalpies of atomisation (kJ mol$^{-1}$): Sc 326, Mn 281, Co 425, Cu 339; Co is highest.
$\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ is $3d^7$ with 3 unpaired electrons: $\mu=\sqrt{3\times5}=\sqrt{15}\approx3.87$ BM, i.e. 4.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
X g of nitrobenzene on nitration gave 4.2 g of m-dinitrobenzene.
X = __________ g. (nearest integer)
[Given : molar mass (in g mol$^{-1}$) C : 12, H : 1, O : 16, N : 14]
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2}$ (123 g mol$^{-1}$) $\rightarrow$ $\mathrm{C_6H_4(NO_2)_2}$ (168 g mol$^{-1}$), 1 : 1.
Moles of product $=\dfrac{4.2}{168}=0.025$; $X=0.025\times123=3.075\approx3$ g.

questions.text: The total number of structural isomers possible for the substituted benzene derivatives with the molecular formula $\mathrm{C_9H_{12}}$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Three carbons outside the ring: propylbenzene and isopropylbenzene (2); ethylmethylbenzenes, ortho, meta, para (3); trimethylbenzenes 1,2,3-, 1,2,4- and 1,3,5- (3).
Total $=8$.
